    Horizon scanning for invasion risk

    Source: R/inv-biosecurity.R
    inv_horizon_scan.Rd

    Combines expert scores for candidate species into an overall risk score and rank, following the consensus approach of Roy et al. (2014). Scores for criteria such as likelihood of arrival, establishment, spread and impact are combined by product, geometric mean or sum. With several assessors, scores are first aggregated by the median for each species and criterion and their spread is reported as a measure of disagreement.

    Usage

    inv_horizon_scan(
  .data,
  ...,
  species,
  assessor = NULL,
  method = c("product", "geometric_mean", "sum"),
  score_range = c(1, 5),
  thresholds = c(1/3, 2/3)
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per species (or per species and assessor).

    ...

    <tidy-select> Criterion columns with numeric scores.

    species

    <tidy-select> Column with the species.

    assessor

    <tidy-select> Optional column with the assessor.

    method

    How to combine criteria: "product", "geometric_mean" or "sum".

    score_range

    Numeric vector of length two with the minimum and maximum possible score of each criterion. Used to scale the overall score to 0 to 1.

    thresholds

    Two cut points on the scaled score separating "low", "medium" and "high" priority.

    Value

    A tibble with one row per species, sorted by rank: the median score for each criterion, n_assessors, disagreement (mean across criteria of the standard deviation among assessors; NA with one assessor), score, scaled_score, rank and priority.

    References

    Roy, H. E., Peyton, J., Aldridge, D. C. et al. (2014). Horizon scanning for invasive alien species with the potential to threaten biodiversity in Great Britain. Global Change Biology, 20, 3859-3871. doi:10.1111/gcb.12603

    Examples

    inv_horizon_scan(inv_horizon, arrival, establishment, impact,
  species = species, assessor = assessor)
